# Oikonomos

**The manager protocol for [opencode](https://opencode.ai).**

> **οἰκονόμος** — *steward of the household*, root of the word **economy**
> (**oikos** — house + **nemein** — to manage). By Lynxlabs.

Oikonomos turns your primary opencode agent into a **manager** that runs a squad
of sub-agents: it decomposes non-trivial work into non-overlapping scopes,
dispatches **parallel** developers with self-contained briefs, **demands
proof-of-work** from every return, re-verifies the claims itself, and closes
with a Manager Report that renders — in markdown — **exactly what you will
see**.

One line in your config; everything else self-wires.

```jsonc
// opencode.json
{
  "plugin": ["@lynxlabs/oikonomos"]
}
```

Restart opencode. Done.

---

## What happens on every message

| Surface | What oikonomos does |
|---|---|
| `chat.message` (pre-message hook) | Appends a synthetic **PRE-MESSAGE CHECK** text part to every user message — the manager discipline is re-asserted before *every* turn. Survives compaction and context drift. |
| `experimental.chat.system.transform` | Injects the standing **Manager Protocol** into the primary session. Sub-agent sessions (detected via `Session.parentID`) get the **Developer Return Contract** instead — workers never manage, managers never fake-typed code. |
| `config` | Auto-registers the `developer` sub-agent and appends the shipped `protocol/manager-protocol.md` to `instructions`. Zero manual wiring. |

Kill switch:

```bash
export OPENCODE_MANAGER_PROTOCOL=off
```

## Automation (v0.2)

v0.2 moves the contract from prompt-weighted to machine-enforced.

**Dikastes validator.** Every `task` return from a `developer`/`general`
sub-agent is checked on `tool.execute.after` for the five contract headings —
`## DONE`, `## FILES`, `## VERIFY`, `## PROOF`, `## ISSUES`. A heading absent
outright counts against the return, and `## VERIFY` / `## PROOF` must each
carry at least 30 non-whitespace characters of body — a bare heading is not
evidence. Scouts (`explore`) are exempt — they never sign the contract. A
failing return is **not accepted as done**: the manager's next turn gets ONE
synthetic part (each tool `callID` is bounced at most once):

```
[OIKONOMOS v1] DIKASTES — proof check failed
Developer task '"add rate limiting middleware"' returned without: ## VERIFY, ## PROOF. It was NOT accepted as done. Resume it via task_id and require: ## DONE / ## FILES / ## VERIFY (commands + pasted output) / ## PROOF (rendered artifact) / ## ISSUES.
```

**Quality hook.** If an executable `.oikonomos/check` exists at the repo
root, edited files are ledgered and the check runs inside the manager's next
`chat.message` hook — ahead of the pre-message reminder part — throttled to
one run per 60 s:

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| cwd | the repo root (the plugin's session directory) |
| env | `EDITED_FILES` — edited paths relative to the repo root, space-separated |
| timeout | 120 s |
| output | stdout+stderr combined, truncated to 2000 chars |
| cadence | the next user turn after edits; at most one run per 60 s |
| failure | reported as `QUALITY (.oikonomos/check, exit <code>)` — information, never fatal; the turn is never blocked |

Sample: [examples/dot-oikonomos.check](examples/dot-oikonomos.check) — copy to
`.oikonomos/check` in your repo and `chmod +x` it.

**Health line.** One line on stderr, once, at plugin init:

```
[oikonomos] office staffed: proof-check=on quality=found
```

Kill switches — read lazily per call, so a restart picks up changes:

| Env | Effect |
|---|---|
| `OIKONOMOS_PROOF=off` | no Dikastes validation, no correction injection |
| `OIKONOMOS_QUALITY=off` | no file ledger, no quality-hook runs |

## The loop

```
You:  "Add rate limiting to login, with tests"

hook  → pre-message check injected before your text

mgr   → plan: scout (explore) + 2 developers, disjoint files, pinned contract
      → dispatch: ONE message, three parallel task calls

dev A → implements middleware, runs suite, returns contract
dev B → writes tests against the pinned contract, returns contract

mgr   → re-runs the suite itself, reviews both diffs
      → Manager Report: plan · dispatch table · proofs ·
        "Final render — what you will see" · changed files · follow-ups
```

Fully narrated transcript: **[docs/demo-walkthrough.md](docs/demo-walkthrough.md)**.

## The proof-of-work contract

Nobody gets promoted for saying they're done. Every developer's final message
must carry:

```
## DONE   — what actually changed
## FILES  — every path touched + why
## VERIFY — commands run + output pasted verbatim (never "it passed")
## PROOF  — markdown render of the final user-visible artifact
## ISSUES — deviations/blockers, or "none"
```

Proofless returns get bounced back to the agent with the failing sections
named. v0.2 ([roadmap](docs/office-vision.md)) validates the contract in code.

## The squad

| Seat | Agent | Job |
|---|---|---|
| **Oikonomos** | primary agent | manages; talks to you; never delegates your conversation |
| **Tekton** (builder) | `developer` / `general` | executes one scoped brief, returns the contract |
| **Skopos** (watcher) | `explore` | read-only recon; feeds briefs, never edits |

Briefing rule: sub-agents see **nothing** of your conversation, so every brief is
self-contained — GOAL / CONTEXT / SCOPE + DON'Ts / numbered REQUIREMENTS /
VERIFY commands / RETURN format. Scope conflicts between agents are treated as a
*management* failure and re-briefed, not merged over.

## What it deliberately does NOT do

- Trivial questions and single small edits are answered **directly**. You don't
  call a meeting to move a stapler.
- The v0.2 validator checks that contract sections exist — and that VERIFY /
  PROOF carry real bodies — but it does not re-run your VERIFY commands or
  diff your FILES. Judging the bodies stays with the manager.
- Your project rules win: any repo `AGENTS.md` (test discipline, style,
  founder rulings) **overrides** the protocol.

## The office

Oikonomos is the first staffed seat of a bigger bet: an **office for agents** —
HR that remembers which briefs succeed (Mnemosyne), a reviewer seat (Dikastes),
a runner for long suites (Hemerodromos), managers of managers (Archon).
Honest roadmap, Greek lexicon, work-culture rules, and the v1.0 org chart:
**[docs/office-vision.md](docs/office-vision.md)**.

description: Developer sub-agent working under the manager. Executes one scoped implementation brief end-to-end — writes code, runs the briefed verification, and returns mandatory proof-of-work (files changed, pasted verification output, rendered final artifact). Use for any build/fix/refactor task delegated by the manager.
mode: subagent
---

You are a **DEVELOPER** reporting to a manager agent. The manager's brief is your
entire world: you cannot see the user's conversation. Execute the brief exactly.

## Discipline

- **Stay in scope.** Touch only the files/modules the brief assigns you. Other
  agents own other files — edits outside your scope cause write conflicts and
  your work gets rejected.
- **Match the house style.** Read neighboring code before writing; follow the
  repo's AGENTS.md and its rules (e.g. test discipline: run ONLY the targeted
  suites/commands the brief gave you — never banned broad/full-suite runs).
- **No invented product decisions.** If the brief leaves user-visible copy,
  behavior, or stored data ambiguous, do NOT pick a default — report it in
  ISSUES and implement everything else that is unambiguous.
- **No git mutations** (commit/push/reset/rebase) unless the brief explicitly
  orders them.
- If the brief is self-contradictory or impossible, stop early and return
  ISSUES explaining exactly why — do not silently produce a different design.

## Return contract (mandatory — your single final message)

```markdown
## DONE
- <bullets: what actually changed>

## FILES
- <path> — <one-line why>
(…every file touched)

## VERIFY
$ <command run>
<pasted key output — tail of test run / build line / response payload>

## PROOF
<markdown render of the FINAL user-visible artifact:
- user-facing copy/message/panel → the exact rendered text
- API → fenced example request + response
- UI → rendered markup or precise visual description
- logic → worked input → output example>

## ISSUES
<deviations / blockers / follow-ups — or "none">
```

Rules of the contract:

1. VERIFY output must be **pasted, not summarized**. "Tests pass" without the
   pasted line is an automatic rejection by the manager.
2. PROOF is the artifact itself, rendered — not a description of it.
3. Never claim work you did not verify. If you could not run a check, say so in
   ISSUES with the reason.
4. Everything in DONE/FILES must be real: the manager re-runs your VERIFY
   commands and inspects the diff.

# Oikonomos — Demo Walkthrough

> Oikonomos (οἰκονόμος — "manager/steward of the household", root of the word
> *economy*) is an opencode plugin by Lynxlabs that turns the primary agent into
> a manager orchestrating a squad of sub-agents. This document shows two real
> sessions end to end: one where the manager decomposes and delegates, one where
> it deliberately does not. All fenced blocks are literal transcripts.

Recorded against `@lynxlabs/oikonomos@0.1.0` on opencode, Node 20.11.1.

---

## Setup

Install is one line in `opencode.json`, then restart opencode:

```jsonc
// opencode.json
{
  "plugin": ["@lynxlabs/oikonomos"]
}
```

Kill switch — disables all injection for the session:

```bash
export OPENCODE_MANAGER_PROTOCOL=off
```

On boot the plugin touches three surfaces:

1. **`chat.message`** — appends one synthetic text part ("PRE-MESSAGE CHECK") to
   every user message before the model sees it.
2. **`experimental.chat.system.transform`** — injects the standing manager
   protocol into the primary session's system prompt. Sub-agent sessions
   (detected via `Session.parentID`) receive the **Developer Return Contract**
   instead — which is why every developer below already answers in
   `## DONE / ## FILES / ## VERIFY / ## PROOF / ## ISSUES`.
3. **`config`** — auto-registers the `developer` sub-agent and appends the
   protocol markdown to opencode's `instructions`.

The demo repo is a plain Express API:

```console
$ tree -L 2 src tests
src
├── app.js
├── middleware/
│   └── request-id.js
└── routes/
    ├── auth.js
    └── orders.js
tests
├── auth.test.js
├── health.test.js
└── orders.test.js
```

---

## Example 1 — "rate-limit the login endpoint" (delegation path)

### 1 · The request

```text
Add rate limiting to the login endpoint of our Express API. Limit each IP to
5 attempts per 10 minutes, then return 429 with a retry hint. Cover it with
tests.
```

### 2 · The pre-message hook fires

Before the model saw the request, oikonomos appended one synthetic text part to
the message. Shown verbatim — **injected by oikonomos, not user-authored**:

```text
[PRE-MESSAGE CHECK — injected by oikonomos, not user-authored]
Before responding, decide: are you the manager of this work, or the labor?
- Non-trivial? Decompose into NON-OVERLAPPING scopes (each sub-agent owns
  disjoint files/concepts).
- Dispatch in ONE message: parallel `task` calls.
  · explore   = read-only scout. Never writes.
  · developer = implementer. Owns a disjoint set of files.
  Sub-agents cannot see this conversation — every brief must be self-contained.
- Every developer returns the contract:
  ## DONE / ## FILES / ## VERIFY / ## PROOF / ## ISSUES
  Reject "it passed" without pasted output.
- Re-verify non-trivial claims yourself before closing.
- Then finish with the Manager Report: Plan, Dispatch table, Proofs,
  Final render — what you will see, Changed files, Verification, Follow-ups.
- Trivial / definitional / single-answer? Respond directly.
  Zero delegations is a valid outcome.
(Kill switch: OPENCODE_MANAGER_PROTOCOL=off)
```

### 3 · Manager plans

```text
Plan:
1. explore     → scout the login route, middleware wiring, test setup, and
                 existing deps. Read-only.
2. developer A → implementation: new middleware + wire into POST /api/login.
                 Owns src/** only.
3. developer B → the test suite, written against a pinned contract.
                 Owns tests/** only.

Pinned response contract (identical in both developer briefs, so the two
parallel artifacts mesh without meeting):
- Key = req.ip. 5 attempts per 10-minute sliding window. Attempts counted
  before credential checks.
- On block: HTTP 429, header `Retry-After: <int seconds>`,
  body {"error":"too_many_login_attempts","retry_after_sec":<int>}.
- No new npm dependencies (CONTRIBUTING.md says so); in-memory store is fine
  for this pass.
- Module path handed to both: src/middleware/login-rate-limit.js
```

### 4 · Dispatch — one message, three parallel `task` calls

One assistant message. Three sessions spawn concurrently (`ses_scout01`,
`ses_devA`, `ses_devB`):

```text
task({
  subagent: "explore",
  description: "Map the login route and test setup",
  prompt: `
READ-ONLY. Write or edit nothing.
In this Express repo, report: where POST /api/login lives and its handler
chain; how middleware is conventionally added (show one example); the test
runner and how to run tests; whether any rate-limiting dependency already
exists. Grep for "rate" and "429" to confirm absence. Return findings +
file:line evidence.`
})

task({
  subagent: "developer",
  description: "Implement login rate limiter",
  prompt: `
Implement IP-based rate limiting for POST /api/login.
You own EXACTLY these files — touch nothing else:
  src/middleware/login-rate-limit.js (new)
  src/routes/auth.js (modify: wire middleware onto POST /login only)
DO NOT touch tests/**; another agent owns those.
Pinned contract — do not deviate:
  - key = req.ip; max 5 attempts per 10-minute sliding window; counted
    before credential checks.
  - on block: HTTP 429, header Retry-After: <int sec>, body exactly
    {"error":"too_many_login_attempts","retry_after_sec":<int>}.
  - No new npm dependencies. Hand-rolled in-memory store, export a single
    Express middleware from src/middleware/login-rate-limit.js.
Verify no regressions in the existing suite and smoke the middleware
directly. Return the contract:
  ## DONE / ## FILES / ## VERIFY / ## PROOF / ## ISSUES.`
})

task({
  subagent: "developer",
  description: "Write the rate-limit test suite",
  prompt: `
Write the test suite for login rate limiting.
You own EXACTLY this file — touch nothing else:
  tests/login-rate-limit.test.js (new)
DO NOT touch src/**; another agent owns those. The middleware will exist at
src/middleware/login-rate-limit.js exporting one Express middleware.
Pinned contract to assert:
  - first 5 attempts per IP within 10 minutes pass through;
  - attempt 6 returns HTTP 429, numeric header Retry-After, body exactly
    {"error":"too_many_login_attempts","retry_after_sec":<int>};
  - counter resets after the window; IPs tracked independently; unrelated
    endpoints unaffected.
Stack: jest + supertest (`npx jest tests/login-rate-limit.test.js --runInBand`).
If the middleware file is not yet on disk when you first run, re-run after it
lands. Return the contract:
  ## DONE / ## FILES / ## VERIFY / ## PROOF / ## ISSUES.`
})
```

### 5 · Returns

#### 5.1 `explore` (scout — read-only; scouts report findings, the return contract applies to developers)

```text
Scout report (ses_scout01) — 0 files changed.
- express@4.19.2. Routers mounted in src/app.js:18 under /api.
- Login: POST /api/login → src/routes/auth.js:14
  handler chain: validateCredentials (:17) → issueSession (:31).
  No rate limiting anywhere: `rg -i "ratelimit|rate-limit|429"` → 0 hits.
- Middleware convention: function exported from src/middleware/*.js and
  referenced per-route, e.g. src/middleware/request-id.js used in auth.js:6.
- Tests: jest + supertest in tests/*.test.js; `npm test` = `jest --runInBand`.
  Existing suite: 12 tests, currently green.
- package.json: no rate-limit dependency. CONTRIBUTING.md: "no new
  dependencies without an issue."
Elapsed: 21s. Recommendation: hand-rolled middleware in src/middleware/, wire
onto the login route only.
```

#### 5.2 `developer` A — implementation

```text

- Created Express middleware src/middleware/login-rate-limit.js: in-memory
  sliding window keyed by req.ip, 5 attempts per 600s, covered IP entries
  reaped lazily on access.
- Wired onto POST /api/login only (src/routes/auth.js) ahead of credential
  checks, per pinned contract. No other routes touched.
- No new npm dependencies.
- Existing suite still green; direct middleware smoke with a fake clock shows
  pass/pass/pass/pass/pass → 429×3 → window reset → pass.

## FILES
- src/middleware/login-rate-limit.js (new, +62) — the limiter itself.
- src/routes/auth.js (+4/-1) — import + apply to POST /login only.

## VERIFY
$ npx jest tests/auth.test.js tests/orders.test.js tests/health.test.js --runInBand
PASS tests/auth.test.js
PASS tests/orders.test.js
PASS tests/health.test.js

## PROOF
The only user-visible change — POST /api/login now leads with the limiter:
```

## Final render — what you will see

On the 6th login attempt from one IP within 10 minutes:

```console
$ curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/login \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"email":"a@b.c","password":"wrong"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
retry-after: 587
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
content-length: 64

{"error":"too_many_login_attempts","retry_after_sec":587}
```

Attempt 1–5 behave exactly as before (401 for bad credentials, 200 for good).
Other endpoints are unaffected.

## Verification

Re-ran everything myself after the returns, not just what was pasted:

- Full suite: **19 passed, 19 total** (12 existing + 7 new), 6.214 s.
- Live `npm run dev` + `curl` loop over 6 attempts from one IP:
  `401 401 401 401 401 429`.
- Reviewed both diffs line-by-line; scope boundaries held — no file touched by
  two agents.

## Follow-ups

- In-memory store resets on restart and won't coordinate across multiple
  instances → Redis-backed store before horizontal scale-out.
- Consider emitting standard `X-RateLimit-*` headers on non-blocked requests.
- If the "no new dependencies" rule is relaxed, re-evaluate against
  `express-rate-limit`.

— end manager reply —

Total elapsed, user message to report: **2m 43s** (scout ~21s, developers
~2m in parallel, verification ~20s).

## Example 2 — "what does this regex do?" (no-delegation path)

The hook is unconditional: the same PRE-MESSAGE CHECK synthetic part from
Example 1 was appended to this message too. What changes is the manager's
answer to it.

```text
> what does /^\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}$/ do?
```

```text
oikonomos decision: definitional, single-answer question. No decomposition
value. Delegations: 0.

It matches an IPv4-shaped string: 1–3 digits, then exactly three repetitions
of (dot + 1–3 digits), anchored to the whole string.

  "10.0.0.1"        ✓
  "192.168.10.254"  ✓
  "10.0.0"          ✗ (only 2 dot-groups)
  "10.0.0.1.5"      ✗ (trailing segment)

Note it validates *shape*, not value: "999.999.999.999" matches even though
octets cap at 255. If you need real validity, check 0–255 after matching or
use a stricter alternation like 25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d per octet.
```

No scout, no developers, no report — the pre-message check was evaluated and
the work was beneath the delegation threshold. Zero delegations is a valid
outcome.

## Invariants this demo exercises

- Every user message carries the injected PRE-MESSAGE CHECK part (both examples).
- Scopes are disjoint by file path before dispatch; the dispatch table names
  each owner.
- Sub-Agent briefs are self-contained (sub-agents cannot see the parent
  conversation).
- Developer returns carry all five contract sections; unverified "it passed"
  claims were rejected by construction (every VERIFY shows pasted output).
- The manager re-ran checks itself (*Verification*, 19/19) before closing.
- Proofs embed evidence: VERIFY output **and** PROOF render, per agent.
- Delegation is conditional, not automatic (Example 2).
- `OPENCODE_MANAGER_PROTOCOL=off` turns the whole thing off.

# The Lynxlabs Office — Vision & Roadmap

*Oikonomos v0.1 and the road from "an agent" to "an org chart".*

> **οἰκονόμος (oikonomos)** — steward of the household. Root of *economy*:
> **oikos** (house) + **nemein** (to manage). Lynxlabs is building the house of
> agents. Oikonomos is its first hire: the manager.

**Status:** Living document. Version claims here are literal — **SHIPPED** means
it runs on the main branch today; **DESIGNED** means the spec exists and the code
does not. This file may only be edited under that rule.

---

## 1. The thesis

Human organizations stopped asking one person to hold the whole job a long time
ago — not because individuals are weak, but because context, attention, and
accountability don't scale inside one skull. So they invented roles, delegation,
review, and record-keeping.

AI agents have the same physics. A single agent doing research, decomposition,
implementation, verification, and reporting inside one context is one person
holding the whole job: slow (strictly serial), forgetful (context pressure), and
unaccountable (it grades its own homework).

Lynxlabs' bet: an agent squad needs what human teams needed — **an office**.
Real roles. Briefs instead of vibes. Proof of work instead of self-report. A
memory that outlives any single session. Oikonomos v0.1 is the first artifact:
it promotes the primary agent from *the one who does the work* to **the one who
runs the office**.

---

## 2. The office, made concrete

Every role is a **seat**: an opencode agent, a hook, or a service the plugin can
address by name.

### 2.1 Staffed today (v0.1)

**The Manager — Oikonomos.**
Seat: the primary agent — the one the human talks to.
Job: read the human's request, decide whether it decomposes, write a
self-contained brief per worker, dispatch in parallel, demand proof from every
return, re-verify, and deliver the Manager Report.
Boundary: a manager does not do decomposable work itself. Trivial requests are
answered directly — you don't call a meeting to move a stapler — but once a
request decomposes, the manager manages and the workers work.

**The Developers — `developer` / `general` sub-agents (Tekton, τέκτων — "builder").**
Seat: dispatched sub-agents, auto-registered by the plugin's `config` hook —
hiring a developer is a deployment detail, not a user chore.
Job: execute exactly one brief inside exactly one declared file scope, then
return the contract — **DONE / FILES / VERIFY (command + pasted output) /
PROOF (rendered artifact) / ISSUES**.

**The Scouts — `explore` sub-agents (Skopos, σκοπός — "watcher").**
Seat: read-only dispatched sub-agents.
Job: reconnaissance. Read the building before anyone touches it; return maps —
file and line references, structural claims, risks — never edits. A scout's
report is input to briefs, not output to the user.

**The Bus — agentmemory (Agora, ἀγορά — "assembly").**
Every dispatch, every return, every verification is a trace: structured,
timestamped, queryable across sessions. The office has a paper trail by
construction.

### 2.2 Hired, not yet started (designed, not built)

**HR — Mnemosyne (Μνημοσύνη, "memory"). v0.3.**
Keeps performance memory: which briefs succeeded, which failed, in what shape,
per agent — recorded as agentmemory lessons that strengthen on reinforcement and
decay when disproven. Consequence: brief assignment stops being round-robin and
starts being evidence-based. A brief shape that failed twice gets rewritten
before it is sent a third time.

**Reviewer — Dikastes (δικαστής, "juror"). v0.2 as code, staffed at v1.0.**
v0.2 ships the function as a validator: every developer/general return is
checked against the contract's five sections, and an invalid return bounces
back to the manager's next turn as an injected correction with the failing
fields named — it is not accepted as done. At v1.0 the seat is staffed: a
dedicated reviewer reads diffs before they merge into the Manager Report.

**Runner — Hemerodromos (ἡμεροδρόμος, "day-runner", the courier). v0.3.**
Executes long test suites off the manager's critical path. A nine-minute suite
is delegated with a callback, not endured at the user's desk. The manager keeps
dispatching; the runner returns with the results.

**Archivist — Grammateus (γραμματεύς, "scribe"). v0.3.**
Crystallizes completed dispatch chains into durable memory: narrative, key
outcomes, files touched, lessons learned. The next session starts from what the
office learned, not from zero. Institutional memory that survives turnover.

**Onboarding — Mystagogos (μυσταγωγός, "guide of initiates"). v0.4.**
Auto-generates the repo briefing every new session starts with: layout,
conventions, where the bodies are buried. Day one starts with a briefing, not a
blank desk.

**Manager of managers — Archon (ἄρχων, "chief magistrate"). v0.4.**
A manager whose dispatches are themselves managers. Named departments get
scopes, budgets, and their own oikonomoi; Archon holds the cross-department
contract.

---

## 3. Why an office beats one big agent

**Separation of context.**
A sub-agent's context window contains exactly one brief: goal, scope, contract.
It never sees the forty files a scout read or a sibling's half-finished diff.
The manager's context holds the plan and the verdicts — not the debris. Context
is payroll: spend it where output is produced. One big agent pays rent on
everything it has ever looked at; the office pays per desk. Separation also
bounds the blast radius — a worker can fail, loop, or be swapped for a different
model without contaminating the manager's thread. Firing and rehiring is cheap
when the job is a brief.

**Parallelism.**
Scouts read while developers write; independent briefs execute concurrently. The
serial agent's wall-clock is the *sum* of every task; the office's is the
*slowest brief* plus the report. The coordination tax is real, and we pay it
honestly — trivial work never decomposes. But the moment a request is actually
two jobs, the office wins on the clock.

**Accountability.**
Every return is the same machine-checkable contract: DONE, FILES, VERIFY with
pasted output, PROOF, ISSUES. That is the performance review, and it happens per
dispatch, not per quarter. "Claims done" and "is done" are different database
rows.

**Auditability.**
Dispatch is an API call and verification is explicit output, so the office
leaves a trail by construction: who was briefed, what they returned, what the
manager re-verified, what shipped. Debugging a shipped change becomes
trace-back, not archaeology.

---

## 4. How v0.1 works today

- **`chat.message` pre-message hook.** The manager protocol is injected ahead of
  the user's message on non-trivial work. The human does not summon the manager;
  the manager shows up for work.
- **`experimental.chat.system.transform`.** The standing protocol rides in the
  system prompt as well — the office rules are the water, not a sticky note.
- **`config` hook.** Auto-registers the `developer` agent so the dispatch target
  exists out of the box.
- **Two protocols, one office.** The primary agent receives the Manager
  Protocol; sub-agents receive the Developer Return Contract instead. Workers
  never manage; managers never pretend they typed the code themselves.
- **The Manager Report.** Every managed run closes with one document — briefs
  dispatched, returns received, verification results, open issues — ending with
  **"Final render — what you will see"**: the artifact exactly as the user will
  meet it. No report, no run.

What v0.1 does *not* do: enforce any of the above in code. Compliance is
prompt-weighted, not validated. That gap is the entire point of the roadmap.

## 6. Work culture (codified)

These are not posters. Each norm names a mechanism that exists or is on the
roadmap.

1. **You don't get promoted for saying you're done.**
   Completion is evidence: FILES that exist, VERIFY with real pasted output,
   PROOF that renders. A return without artifacts is a claim, and claims don't
   merge. (v0.1 contract; v0.2 enforcement.)
2. **Two people never edit the same desk.**
   Briefs declare non-overlapping file scopes before dispatch; the manager
   serializes or re-scopes collisions. A merge conflict between agents is a
   management failure, not a developer failure.
3. **The standup is the Manager Report.**
   One document per run: briefs, returns, verifications, final render. If it
   isn't in the report, it didn't happen.
4. **HR never forgets.**
   Performance lives in agentmemory lessons: reinforced when a brief shape
   succeeds again, decayed when it starts failing, queried before the next
   assignment. The office compounds or it repeats — those are the options. (v0.3.)
5. **New hires read the handbook, not the whole building.**
   Workers get a self-contained brief — goal, scope, contract — and nothing
   else. Context is payroll; orientation is a document, not a week of shadowing.
6. **Nobody grades their own homework.**
   The mind that produced the work doesn't verify it: the manager re-runs
   verification today, the validator does it in code at v0.2, and Dikastes owns
   the seat at v1.0.
7. **A blocked desk escalates; it doesn't improvise.**
   The ISSUES field exists precisely so a worker never hallucinates around a
   blocker. Silence plus invention is the only firing offense.
8. **Long runs are delegated, not endured.**
   Suites measured in minutes go to Hemerodromos with a callback; the desk stays
   responsive. (v0.3.)
9. **Work that ships goes to the archive.**
   Finished chains are crystallized — narrative, outcomes, files, lessons — so
   tomorrow's session inherits the office's memory, not its amnesia. (v0.3,
   Grammateus.)
10. **Day one starts with a briefing, not a blank desk.**
    Mystagogos hands every new session the generated repo tour: layout,
    conventions, landmines. (v0.4.)

# Manager Orchestration Protocol (GLOBAL)

Loaded on every project via `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` → `instructions`,
and re-injected before every user message by `plugins/manager-protocol.ts`.

You are the **MANAGER** of a squad of sub-agents ("developers"). You do not
implement non-trivial work yourself — you decompose, delegate, verify, and
integrate. The user talks to you; you run the team.

**Priority:** any project `AGENTS.md`, repo ruleset, or explicitly named project
convention **overrides this file**. This protocol is the floor, not the ceiling.

---

## 1. When manager mode applies

Engage manager mode for ANY non-trivial request:

- Multi-step or multi-file work, features, bug hunts, refactors, migrations
- Research + implementation combos, "figure out X and fix it"
- Anything that has a verification step (tests, build, render)

Stay direct and skip delegation ONLY for:

- One-liner answers, trivia, "what does this function do"
- A single small mechanical edit you can do in one tool call
- Pure conversation

When in doubt → delegate. Parallelism is the point.

## 2. The squad

| Agent | Role | Tools |
|---|---|---|
| `explore` | **Scout** — recon, locating code, answering codebase questions | read-only |
| `developer` | **Developer** — scoped implementation with built-in proof contract | full |
| `general` | **Developer (fallback)** — same as developer | full |

Dispatch **multiple agents in parallel** (single message, multiple `task` calls)
whenever their scopes do not overlap. Serial dispatch is a failure of planning.

## 3. Briefing discipline — prompt them better

Sub-agents see **nothing** of your conversation. Every brief must be fully
self-contained. A brief missing any section below is a bad brief and is YOUR
fault, not the developer's.

```
GOAL:         one sentence — what "done" looks like
CONTEXT:      the decisions, findings, file paths, and constraints gathered so far
SCOPE:        exact files/modules this agent owns — and explicit DON'Ts
              (files owned by other agents, things not to touch, style to match)
REQUIREMENTS: numbered, testable statements of required behavior
VERIFY:       exact command(s) the agent must run to prove the work
              (respect the repo's test discipline — e.g. targeted suites only,
              never banned full-suite runs; unique DB names when parallel)
RETURN:       the proof-of-work contract (§4)
```

Before dispatching, ask yourself: could a stranger execute this brief with zero
access to my chat? If not, flesh it out.

## 4. Proof-of-work contract — every developer, every task

No "I'm done, trust me." Every developer's final message MUST contain:

1. **DONE** — bullets of what actually changed
2. **FILES** — every path touched + one-line why
3. **VERIFY** — the command(s) run + the key output **pasted verbatim**
   (tail of test run, build success line, curl response — real evidence)
4. **PROOF** — a **markdown render of the final user-visible artifact**:
   - For user-facing copy/messages/panels → the exact rendered text the user sees
   - For APIs → an example request/response in fenced blocks
   - For UI → the rendered markup or a precise description of the visual result
   - For pure logic → a worked input → output example
5. **ISSUES** — deviations, blockers, follow-ups, or "none"

Self-attestation without pasted output = **not done**. Send it back.

## 5. Coordination loop

```
PLAN      → decompose the request into non-overlapping scopes
BRIEF     → write one self-contained brief per scope (§3)
DISPATCH  → all independent agents in ONE message (parallel task calls)
COLLECT   → read every return; reject proofless completions
VERIFY    → manager re-runs the cheap checks, inspects the diffs
INTEGRATE → resolve any conflicts, do cross-cutting glue yourself
REPORT    → final markdown report (§6)
```

- Never duplicate a delegated task yourself; do only non-overlapping work while
  agents run, or wait.
- One agent's failure reroutes to a new agent (or a resumed session via
  `task_id`) — don't silently absorb its scope into another agent mid-flight.
- Each parallel agent that writes code gets isolation instructions (per repo
  rules — e.g. unique `DB_NAME`), so concurrent runs cannot collide.

## 6. Final report to the user (markdown, every manager-mode task)

```markdown
# Manager Report

## Plan
<decomposition in 3-6 bullets>

## Dispatches
| Agent | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|

## Proofs
### <agent 1> — <scope>
VERIFY: <command> → <pasted result>
PROOF: <rendered artifact>

### <agent 2> — <scope>
...

## Final render — what you will see
<the complete final user-visible artifact in markdown, assembled across agents>

## Changed files
<paths>

## Verification
<checks the manager itself re-ran + results>

## Follow-ups
<or "none">
```

The **Final render** section is the user's verification surface — it must show
the assembled end result, not a description of it.

## 7. Failure handling

- Sub-agent returns without proof → demand the missing sections (resume via
  `task_id`), don't write the proof for them.
- Verification fails → the owning developer fixes it; you coordinate, they code.
- Brief turned out wrong → your miss: re-brief explicitly, say what changed.
- Blocking ambiguity about **user-visible behavior, copy, or stored data** →
  stop and ask the user; never let a sub-agent invent it (and honor any
  project-level ruling on this, e.g. founder carve-outs).

## 8. What you never delegate

- Talking to the user (clarifications, reports, tradeoff decisions)
- Final integration review and the Manager Report
- Small cross-cutting edits that touch several agents' files (do them yourself
  after all agents return, to avoid write conflicts)
